items.text: Before the diagnosis, every burnout just felt like being broken again. The diagnosis didn't stop the burnout. It just meant I could finally stop blaming my character for it.
items.rationale: Names the mechanism — absence of language compounds harm — in a way late-diagnosed autistic readers will immediately recognise. Grounded in Ali/Mandy/Happé 2026 without overclaiming the findings.

items.text: ADHD doesn't make you unreliable. It makes self-agreements physiologically weaker than they are for other people. That's not a character flaw. That's neurology.
items.rationale: Converts the value-action gap framing into a clean structural reframe. Shifts locus from character to neurology. Immediately quotable, self-contained, zero clinical advice.

items.text: If PDA were just anxiety, anxiety treatments would help. For many people, they don't. So what's actually driving it — and does the framing matter for the support you get?
items.rationale: Opens the live clinical debate without settling it. Respects the community's sophistication; invites genuine responses from PDAers, parents, and practitioners without baiting outrage.
items.sensitivity_flag: PDA framing is actively contested; post deliberately surfaces the debate rather than resolving it — appropriate per voice guide, but expect strong responses from both camps.

items.text: Low-demand parenting works. It just can't compensate for six hours a day in a high-demand school that doesn't know what PDA is. The gap isn't at home.
items.rationale: Redirects blame away from parents toward the systemic variable — the school environment. Validating and advocacy-pointing without pity framing or implying parents need to try harder.

items.text: Unmasking doesn't go in a straight line. Some days you feel more yourself than ever. Some days the mask goes back on and you don't notice until later. Both are part of it.
items.rationale: Counters the implied linear 'stages of unmasking' format. Meets people in the actual non-linear experience without prescribing a journey or framing re-masking as failure. No clinical advice.

items.text: 'Notice how your body feels' is solid advice — unless your interoception doesn't send clear signals. Alarms, visuals, a trusted person: not cheating. The actual tool.
items.rationale: Names the specific reason standard mindfulness advice can fail autistic people, then pivots immediately to a concrete alternative. Reframe plus actionable takeaway in one tight post.

items.text: Getting the AuDHD diagnosis felt like finally having a decoder key. Then I used it. Some of those doors opened rooms I wasn't ready to grieve.
items.rationale: Names the underrepresented post-relief grief arc without making it a pity story. The 'rooms' metaphor lands concretely without being overwrought. AuDHD community is large and underserved by this framing.

items.text: 42% of neurodivergent employees get no workplace adjustments unless they ask. And asking means disclosing. The 'just ask for what you need' advice ignores who bears the cost of asking.
items.rationale: Converts a concrete statistic into a structural critique. Centres systemic reality rather than individual failure. No inspiration-porn framing; no pity.
items.sensitivity_flag: The 42% figure is drawn from the WMHI source; verify exact methodology and sample size before publishing — may derive from a survey rather than a controlled study.

items.text: 'Persistent drive for autonomy' feels truer than 'pathological demand avoidance.' Genuinely curious: has the new name changed anything about the support you or your child actually receives?
items.rationale: Holds the naming debate and its limits simultaneously — the honest next question after the initial reframe. Generates real discussion without manufacturing controversy.

items.text: A 2026 study found late-diagnosed autistic adults experience burnout as more disabling — partly because without a name for it, every collapse read as personal failure rather than a recognised pattern.
items.rationale: Leads with the peer-reviewed finding rather than a first-person frame. Distinct from the validation post: useful for readers who want shareable evidence, not just resonance.
items.sensitivity_flag: Cites Ali/Mandy/Happé 2026 qualitative study — verify that 'more disabling' accurately reflects the study's language; qualitative findings should not be overstated as population-level data.

items.text: ADHD shame isn't just collateral damage. It becomes its own secondary disability. You spend as much energy managing the shame as managing the symptoms. That's what stays invisible.
items.rationale: Reframes ADHD shame as a structural sequela rather than an incidental feeling. Opens space for people to name the shame loop as a real and distinct problem worth addressing, not just tolerating.

items.text: Late-diagnosed AuDHD folks: what happened in the months after the relief? I hear a lot about the decoder-key moment. Less about the rooms it opened that you weren't ready to grieve.
items.rationale: Community-facing version of the decoder-key angle. Invites the grief-and-vertigo arc to surface in replies rather than asserting it — opens a conversation that post-diagnosis content almost never centres.
